Several days ago I began to accumulate long positions in the space - here is what I wrote on @thestreetpro:

Buy Financials

I  view financials/banks as a benefit of market rotation (possibly away from technology).

* Financials, on average, are about  25% off of their 52 week highs.

* Valuations are now reasonable.

* Major money center banks and brokers have spent massive amounts on technology – a lot of which is already “sunken costs. This provides the “best in class” and largest banks (as first adopters to AI) to be differentiated against the broad universe of smaller sized banks (who will not be able to catch up and compete).

* As I see it, the yield curve will be normalizing – benefiting net interest margins and income.

* The slowdown in AI spend (which I anticipate) should elongate the domestic economic cycle – improving the credit outlook and asset growth.

* An improving equity augurs well for capital market activity.

* Finally, while the unrealized losses on their investment portfolio is underwater – the likelihood that interest rates may have peaked augurs well for that line item to appreciate in the time ahead.

真正的行业专家背景买方投资看的当然不只是一个收入和毛利超预期，这都是大概率。要看到这种英伟达顶级的技术路线和工程实现能力，这才是真正的护城河

Jensen Left. Nvidia’s Role as the Central Bank of AI Didn’t.

Nvidia’s first results since Jensen Huang resigned on 12 November answer the obvious question: is it still underwriting the AI build-out? It is, and on a larger scale.

Under interim chief executive Colette Kress, Nvidia reported revenue of $ 115.8bn and guided to $ 130bn. Its maximum exposure under guarantees rose to $ 118bn from $ 108.5bn, including a new $ 9.5bn credit-support line for power and systems, and it has yet to make a single payment on them. Leases and cloud agreements climbed to $ 102bn from $ 74bn. The $ 105bn backstop for OpenAI’s Ohio campus remains. Nvidia funded $ 15.7bn of equity in the quarter, taking this year’s total to $ 58bn.

Kress was candid about why. Neoclouds and frontier labs, she wrote, “are growing faster than their balance sheets and long-term credit profiles can support.” That is a demand problem every supplier would want. Nvidia closes the gap with guarantees, equity and patient credit terms, much as a central bank does for an economy.

The bears will call it circular financing. But a company earning $ 65bn a quarter doesn’t backstop demand it doubts. It underwrites demand it can see.

T. Rowe Sticks to Bearish Treasuries Bet That Fueled Banner 2026

Betting on UK gilts and against US Treasuries since early 2026 is paying off for T. Rowe Price’s Scott Solomon, who isn’t in any hurry to unwind those wagers.

His co-managed $800 million Dynamic Global Bond Fund is up around 5% so far this year, beating 97% of peers and on track for its best annual performance since 2020, according to data tracked by Bloomberg.

Underpinning that return was a basic conviction Solomon and his team maintained through geopolitical turmoil and oil-price swings: That the US economy would keep outpacing other economies, putting pressure on Treasuries. That view was borne out again last week, when a hot US inflation print and hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials set off the worst Treasuries rout since April 2025.

“We’ve stuck with the view of strong growth in the US and not quite as good growth in the rest of the world,” Solomon said in an interview last week. “We did a good job of not necessarily flip-flopping on those views.” (Bloomberg)

text:
Behind Nvidia’s rise to a $5 trillion company was a culture of put-downs, parties and a “royal family,” according to a new Wall Street Journal investigation.

Jensen Huang was known inside the company for being demanding and difficult, and so was his daughter, Madison. She was one of two adult children he brought into the business, along with his son, Spencer. $NVDA - The U.S. Commerce and Justice Departments have released a detailed timeline of their Megaspeed investigation, confirming NVDAs topped selling to the Singapore data-center company in June 2025, when it was placed on Nvidia's internal "no sell" list. 

HERE'S WHAT THE JOINT STATEMENT REVEALS:

2024:Commerce opened an investigation after detecting suspicious activity suggesting possible diversion of sensitive U.S. semiconductors. 

May 2025: Investigators requested Nvidia's records covering direct and indirect sales to Megaspeed. 

June 2025: Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its internal "no sell" list. June 2025: U.S. and Singaporean authorities conducted an on-site inspection of Megaspeed and interviewed its then-CEO, Alice Huang. 

Afterward: The Justice Department took the lead in the criminal investigation. The disclosure comes after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized Commerce for not placing Megaspeed on the U.S. trade blacklist, despite support from four federal agencies. 

Importantly, Nvidia's internal "no sell" list is separate from the government's Entity List. Source: U.S. Commerce and Justice Departments
